pr_title: fix: Fix `set_operation` if the input is sliced and be broadcast

issue_context.title: set_difference gives different result with shifted col vs native col
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [[1,2], [2,3]],
        "b": [None, [1,2]],
    }
)

(df
 .with_columns(pl.col("a").shift(1).alias("shifted_a"))
 .with_columns(
     pl.col("b").list.set_difference("a").alias("b set_diff a"),
     pl.col("shifted_a").list.set_difference("a").alias("shifted a set_diff a")
 ))
```
```
┌───────────┬───────────┬───────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│ a         ┆ b         ┆ shifted_a ┆ b set_diff a ┆ shifted a set_diff a │
│ ---       ┆ ---       ┆ ---       ┆ ---          ┆ ---                  │
│ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] ┆ list[i64]    ┆ list[i64]            │
╞═══════════╪═══════════╪═══════════╪══════════════╪══════════════════════╡
│ [1, 2]    ┆ null      ┆ null      ┆ null         ┆ null                 │
│ [2, 3]    ┆ [1, 2]    ┆ [1, 2]    ┆ [1]          ┆ []                   │
└───────────┴───────────┴───────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────┘
```

### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

set_difference gives different result with shifted col vs native col

### Expected behavior

I expect in this example that the set_difference for `b set_diff a` is the same as `shifted a set_diff a`.  
With the first it equals `[1]` as expected, in the later it equals `[]` which is not the correct result

comments:
This is a weird one for sure.

If we add some more observations then it works

```
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [[1,2], [2,3],[3,4],[5,6]],
        "b": [None, [1,2], [2,3],[3,4]],
    }
)


(df
 .with_columns(pl.col("a").shift(1).alias("shifted_a"))
 .with_columns(
     pl.col("b").list.set_difference("a").alias("b set_diff a"),
     pl.col("shifted_a").list.set_difference("a").alias("shifted a set_diff a")
 ))
```

Not sure why it fails with just 2 rows but not 3 or 4. I haven't checked the other set functions.

I marked as high priority since wrong results seem like they would be high but it's not so innocuous as 1+1=3 so not critical.
Thanks for reporting this! Will take a look.

review_comments: We iterate the whole value array if the input on this side should be broadcast. But If the input was a `sliced` list, this will produce wrong results as `slice` over `ListArray` will not slice the underlying value array.
Ai, right. That's a painful one. The fact that lists slice the offset has hit us more often. :/
